subject: Swap It Sustainable Fashion Business Model
overview: Host Danielle Balocca interviewed Stephanie Johnson, owner of the Medford business Swap It, regarding her store's circular clothing exchange model and focus on environmental sustainability.

items.title: Pride t-shirt fundraiser
items.summary: Announced t-shirt sales for Medford's upcoming Pride events with proceeds benefiting the Medford High School GSA.

items.title: Local business spotlight
items.summary: Introduced Stephanie Johnson, owner of Swap It, who recommended Real Gusto in Medford Square as a local dining favorite.

items.title: Clothing swap concept and inclusion
items.summary: Explained the store's model where customers swap items instead of buying or consigning, which serves anyone who wears women's clothing including the trans community.

items.title: Membership structure and styling services
items.summary: Detailed the $147 annual membership for unlimited swaps and the availability of personal styling sessions to build customer confidence.

items.title: Mission and environmental origins
items.summary: Discussed the owner's background in environmental advocacy and her goal to reduce textile waste in landfills by formalizing the local swap economy.

items.title: Body positivity and sizeless organization
items.summary: Described the practice of organizing inventory by style rather than size labels to help customers overcome body image issues and find better-fitting pieces.

items.title: Community events and contact information
items.summary: Highlighted the upcoming All About Pants event and directed listeners to the business website for free trial swaps.
